sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 11891 of 2023
Applicant :- Chhotki

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Sectt. Lko
Counsel for Applicant :- Arvind Kumar,Avinash Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. In terms of the Fir, it was alleged that the sister of the informant was married to the son of the
applicant in the year 2018, subsequently, it was informed that the sister of the informant has died on
account of suicide on 28.12.2022.
3.  The counsel for the applicant argues that there are no post mortem report on record in as much as that it was a natural death.

He further argues that this fact was given effect by the informant in the statement, which is on record as Annexure No. 3 that the funeral was performed, subsequently the Chhotki vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

entities.text: Chhotki vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further argued that the applicant is the mother in law of the deceased and has no criminal history, as such, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the fact that even as per the allegation, there is no allegation that soon before the death, the deceased was subjected to any mental or physical harassment in relation to the demand of dowry at the instance of the applicant coupled with the fact that the applicant has separate living and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Chhotki be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 572 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mohammadpur Khala, District Barabanki, on her furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which she is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.2.2024 Arun  Chhotki vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39317233/
